knowledge:
- key_parameters: sj=A matrix or data frame containing splice junction coordinates and split-read support (columns: chr, start, end, uniq.reads) ;; gen=A SCANVIS-readable gene annotation list containing EXONS, INTRONS, GENES, and GENES.merged ;; Rcut=Read cut-off threshold for filtering splice junctions ;; bam=Optional URL or path to a BAM file to compute Relative Read-Coverage (RRC) scores for Novel Exons or overlay read profiles ;; samtools=Path to the executable samtools, required if bam is provided ;; p=Padding parameter in base pairs to map variants near gene borders (default is 0) ;; roi=Region of interest defined as a gene name, vector of gene names, or genomic coordinates ;; full.annot=Logical indicating whether to display full annotation details in sashimi plots ;; SJ.special=A matrix of specific splice junctions to highlight in the visualization
- alternatives: STAR aligner is mentioned as the tool of choice for predetermining splice junctions and read support before running SCANVIS.
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing RNA-seq splice junctions to identify and categorize unannotated splice events (such as exon-skipping, alternative 5'/3' splice sites, isoform switches, and novel exons), score their relative read support, link them to mutations/variants, and visualize them in publication-ready sashimi plots.
- pitfalls: Supplying a BAM file to compute RRC scores or overlay read profiles significantly increases computation time and memory requirements. If a BAM file is provided, the samtools parameter must not be NULL and must point to a valid executable samtools path. Unannotated splice junctions (USJs) are often frequent and have poor read support, which may represent alignment artifacts; SCANVIS uses Relative Read Support (RRS) relative to annotated SJs to mitigate this.

workflows.name: splice_junction_analysis_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Scan, score, and annotate splice junctions, link them to genomic variants, and visualize the results using sashimi plots.
input: sj_table.txt (Tab-delimited file containing splice junction coordinates and unique read counts)
variants.vcf (VCF or tab-delimited file containing genomic coordinates of variants and mutation details)
gtf_annotation.gtf (GTF file used to generate SCANVIS-readable gene annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the SCANVIS package and example datasets or generate a SCANVIS-readable annotation object ;; 2. Scan and score splice junctions using SCANVISscan ;; 3. Map genomic variants to the scanned splice junctions using SCANVISlinkvar ;; 4. Visualize splice junctions and variants in a region of interest using SCANVISvisual
workflows.code:
library(SCANVIS)
data(SCANVISexamples)
names(gen19)
head(gbm3)
gbm3.scn<-SCANVISscan(sj=gbm3,gen=gen19,Rcut=5,bam=NULL,samtools=NULL)
head(gbm3.scn)
head(gbm3.vcf)
gbm3.scnv<-SCANVISlinkvar(gbm3.scn,gbm3.vcf,gen19)
gbm3.scnv[10:23,]
gbm3.scnvp<-SCANVISlinkvar(gbm3.scn,gbm3.vcf,gen19,p=100)
table(gbm3.scnv[,'passedMUT'])
table(gbm3.scnvp[,'passedMUT'])
par(mfrow=c(2,1),mar=c(1,1,1,1))
vis.lusc1<-SCANVISvisual('PPA2',gen19,LUSC[[1]],TITLE=names(LUSC)[1],full.annot=TRUE,bam=NULL,samtools=NULL)
vis.lusc2<-SCANVISvisual('PPA2',gen19,LUSC[[2]],TITLE=names(LUSC)[2],full.annot=TRUE,bam=NULL,samtools=NULL,USJ='RRS')
ASJ<-tail(vis.lusc2[[2]])[,1:3]
c2<-SCANVISvisual('PPA2',gen19,LUSC[[2]],TITLE=names(LUSC)[2],full.annot=TRUE,SJ.special=ASJ)
vis.lusc.merged<-SCANVISvisual('PPA2',gen19,LUSC,TITLE='Two LUSC samples, merged',full.annot=TRUE)
